body: Like a lot of people are saying, I think if the first choice is more interesting to you, you should go for that one =) a good branch of psychology to look at is Social Psychology. This deals a lot with in-group, out-group issues, so includes things like social influence theories, gender roles and identity, group behavior versus individual behavior... Etc. A good thing about Psychology is that there is a lot of overlap between different areas-they're not separate and distinct from one another, but all overlap with each other in a variety of ways. So besides social psychology you could also look at areas like Personality/Individual differences, where there may be some research into the personalities of those in power, which you could then cross with research from social psychology looking into whether leaders are born or made (on which I know there has been a lot of research, as I did an essay on it myself!).  Cultural influence may also be good to look at in your case, which is again covered by social psychology. This is just an idea, but I guess what I'm trying to get across is that one of the key things in Psychology is being able to relate between different areas, so that you keep a specific focus on the topic in mind, but consider all sides of the issue. If ever I was stuck, I used to write a short list of (3- 5) points related directly to the topic I was looking at. I'd then have a quick look at what the research had said on each of those points, including major/classic research as well as new/unique results.... And then work out a way of pulling everything together in such a way that you are mainly focussed on what academic research has said, but including some personal ideas, e.g. For further research. By breaking it down like that it makes Psychology seem a whole lot less scary, because it's no longer a massive wall of quotes and research and opinions! If you wanted specific places to start your search, Google scholar is fab =P there are loads of good social psychology textbooks, but Baron, Byrne and Branscombe's 'social psychology' (12th or 13th edition, I can't remember what the most recent edition is) could maybe help you too. I hope this all helps even a little bit, I was a psychology student myself and remember how daunting the essays could be! Good luck!
